name: Ceftriaxone for Injection IP (1g)
main_cause: Acute Bacterial Meningitis, Typhoid Fever, Severe CAP, Complicated Urosepsis
main_action: Binds and acylates PBP-3 to block peptidoglycan cross-linking and trigger bacterial cell lysis.
reconstitution_and_dilution: Dissolve 1g in 10 mL Sterile Water for IV. For IM, reconstitute with 3.5 mL 1% Lidocaine. NEVER use calcium-containing diluents.
infusion_rate_and_timing: 1g to 2g once every 24 hours (or 2g q12h in meningitis).
important_cautions: Strict Incompatibility: Never mix or co-infuse with calcium solutions (Ringer's Lactate) due to fatal crystalline precipitation.
Contraindicated in hyperbilirubinemic neonates due to kernicterus risk.

name: Linezolid Injection (2mg/mL, 600mg/300mL)
main_cause: HAP/VAP caused by MRSA, Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus (VRE) bacteremia
main_action: Binds 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit, preventing 70S initiation complex assembly and halting toxin release.
routes_of_administration: Slow IV Piggyback Infusion over 30 to 120 minutes
reconstitution_and_dilution: Ready-to-use 300 mL container (600 mg). Do not dilute further.
infusion_rate_and_timing: 600 mg IV every 12 hours infused over 60 minutes.
important_cautions: Serotonin Syndrome risk: Weak reversible MAO-inhibitor; avoid concurrent SSRIs/SNRIs.
Check weekly CBC for myelosuppression if therapy extends past 10–14 days.
